answer: Lock each new agent's earnings in a vesting schedule that only unlocks after months of graded, useful work. Reputation builds at a glacier pace, so a swarm of fake identities sits on frozen rewards. To profit, an attacker must keep every puppet answering fresh tasks for the whole period, paying compute for each one, while a single detected comet-like burst of copied answers forfeits the unvested pile. Trust is a walnut: slow to grow, hard to crack.
